html:
The dispute between India and Pakistan over Kashmir began in October 1947, in the first weeks after the Partition, and continues.

Kashmir was a princely state with a Muslim majority and a Hindu ruler, Maharaja Hari Singh, who put off a choice between the two new countries. A revolt began in Poonch in the west. On 22 October 1947, Pashtun tribesmen from Pakistan's northwest, with Pakistani help, invaded and approached Srinagar, looting Baramulla on the way.

Hari Singh asked India for help and signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October. Nehru sent troops by air the next day. The war ran for over a year, until a UN-arranged ceasefire on 1 January 1949. India got about two thirds, including the valley, and Pakistan the western strip, now Azad Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan. The ceasefire line became the Line of Control.

A UN vote on the people's wishes was promised but never held. India and Pakistan fought over it again in 1965 and 1999, and a separatist insurgency began in 1989 and 1990, leading to the exodus of Kashmiri Pandits.
sum: The dispute between India and Pakistan over Kashmir began in October 1947, in the first weeks after the Partition, and continues.
